evidence_kind: nonproduction native aaPanel PHP85 guarded manual FPM integration and real two-site HTTP test
candidate: 0.1.3 development ZIP; no release or production installation

environment.isolation: disposable QCOW2 overlay on retained local QEMU lab; no production targets

fault_injection.mechanism: test-specific injected transient exception after actual native FPM candidate reload; production code uses real hooks
fault_injection.first_permanent_fault: Persistent double-reload failure correctly returned uncertain, kept recovery journal; manually restored via approved endpoint and exact original bytes
fault_injection.single_transient_fault: After forward FPM reload an injected exception was raised; automatic backup restore, second real reload, baseline-specific FPM runtime verification and two-site PHP HTTP health passed

limitations: The aaPanel endpoint was invoked as an installed Python class with a Flask test request context; actual interactive browser full-admin CSRF and restricted-role session replay were not exercised in this integration test.
File attribution does not prove all effective Nginx include/routing consumers, nor all external FastCGI clients.
Product runtime hooks verify php-fpm -tt values, PID and Unix socket. Two-site HTTP probes were independent test instrumentation, not an embedded generic per-site health checker.
Only direct one-pool PHP 8.5 aaPanel 8.0.7 Nginx path tested; no Apache or other aaPanel/PHP versions claimed.
This is nonproduction development evidence; no supported public release or production deployment.
One final site mapping check is performed immediately before write but cannot synchronize with arbitrary external aaPanel writers; site reassignment racing after that check remains possible.

PHP-FPM -tt re-parses disk configuration and does not independently expose each already-running child's effective values; runtime verification uses native reload result and PID/socket availability. Full client-level health requires additional monitoring.
Native WriteLog API persistence was positively tested on aaPanel 8.0.7 only; log subsystem failures remain explicitly reported but do not revert an otherwise successful host operation.

native_activity_log.api: public.WriteLog via installed aaPanel 8.0.7 Python backend
native_activity_log.storage_failure_behavior: report audit_logged false without misrepresenting host operation status
